# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# evento_accord - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/evento-accord/2.0.0-alpha.24/evento_accord/

## Expand description

Accord consensus protocol (Apache Cassandra [CEP-15](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/CASSANDRA/CEP-15:+General+Purpose+Transactions)) for evento.

This crate is building toward a new evento [ Executor](https://docs.rs/evento-core/2.0.0-alpha.24/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/evento_core/executor/trait.Executor.html) that turns evento
into a

**leaderless, strictly-serializable, highly-available replicated event store**: events are replicated across

`N = 2f + 1` nodes with a single
global serial order and no elected leader, tolerating `f` failures.See `DESIGN.md` for the full architecture and milestone plan. The crate is
currently at **M0 (skeleton)**: the [ api](https://docs.rs/api/index.html) traits, core types, an in-memory
transport, and a tested Hybrid Logical Clock are in place; the protocol
phases (M1+) are not yet implemented.

[§](https://docs.rs#layering)Layering

```
Executor impl (M5) → Coordinator → protocol core → api traits
                                                    (MessageSink, Topology,
                                                     Clock, Journal, DataStore)
```
The protocol depends only on the [ api](https://docs.rs/api/index.html) traits, each with a deterministic
in-process implementation for testing and a production implementation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [api](https://docs.rs/api/index.html)
- Host-facing trait interfaces, modelled on `accord-core`’s`accord/api`package. The protocol core depends only on these traits; each has a deterministic in-process implementation for the simulation harness and a production implementation (real transport, static-config membership, Fjall/SQL-backed storage).
- [clock](https://docs.rs/clock/index.html)
- Cluster node identity and the Hybrid Logical Clock.
- [executor](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)
- Wiring Accord into evento’s `Executor`
- [failure_](https://docs.rs/failure_detector/index.html)- detector
- Phi-accrual failure detector (Hayashibara et al.).
- [format](https://docs.rs/format/index.html)
- On-the-wire and on-disk record framing: a small, explicit version tag in front of every bitcode payload, so a format change is detectable instead of silently mis-parsed.
- [message](https://docs.rs/message/index.html)
- Wire messages and per-transaction command state.
- [metrics](https://docs.rs/metrics/index.html)
- Lightweight runtime counters for observability.
- [node](https://docs.rs/node/index.html)
- A cluster node: one replica plus the coordinator logic for client writes and for recovering transactions whose coordinator has failed.
- [replica](https://docs.rs/replica/index.html)
- Replica-side consensus state machine.
- [store](https://docs.rs/store/index.html)
- In-memory `DataStore``Journal`
- [tcp](https://docs.rs/tcp/index.html)
- Production transport: length-delimited framed TCP behind the
`MessageSink`
- [transport](https://docs.rs/transport/index.html)
- In-memory `MessageSink`

# rship_entities_nodes - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-entities-nodes/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_entities_nodes/

## Expand description

BindingNode Execution System

This crate provides the infrastructure for executing binding nodes in the scene graph. Each node type is defined using:

- The `#[binding_node]`proc macro on a struct
- `impl StaticAnchors`(static nodes) or- `impl ReactiveAnchors`(dynamic nodes)
- Either `impl PureNode`or`impl CellNode`for execution

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
BindingNodeOutputValue Report
    |
find_executor(node_type)  // String-based lookup
    |
NodeExecutor::Pure(compute) or NodeExecutor::Cell(make_cell)
    |
Cell<BindingDatagram, CellImmutable>
```
[§](https://docs.rs#defining-new-nodes)Defining New Nodes

[§](https://docs.rs#pure-nodes-synchronous-vectorizable)Pure Nodes (synchronous, vectorizable)

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rship_entities_nodes::SchemaToken;
use rship_entities_nodes::{StaticAnchors, PureNode, AnchorDef, anchor};
#[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, pure)]
pub struct GateNode;
impl StaticAnchors for GateNode {
    fn input_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("value", SchemaToken::T), anchor("open", SchemaToken::BOOL)]
    }
    fn output_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("output", SchemaToken::T)]
    }
}
impl PureNode for GateNode {
    fn compute(get_input: &dyn Fn(&str) -> BindingValue, _output_id: &str) -> BindingValue {
        let open = get_input("open").to_bool();
        if open { get_input("value") } else { BindingValue::Null }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#cell-nodes-reactiveasync)Cell Nodes (reactive/async)

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use hyphae::{Cell, CellImmutable, SampleExt, Pipeline, MaterializeDefinite};
#[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, cell)]
pub struct SampleNode;
impl StaticAnchors for SampleNode { ... }
impl CellNode for SampleNode {
    fn make_cell(ctx: NodeExecutionContext) -> impl MaterializeDefinite<BindingDatagram> {
        let trigger = ctx.input_cell("trigger");
        let emitter = ctx.input_cell("emitter");
        emitter.sample(&trigger)
    }
}
```

# evento_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/evento-core/2.0.0-alpha.24/evento_core/

## Expand description

Core types and traits for the Evento event sourcing library.

This crate provides the foundational abstractions for building event-sourced applications with Evento. It defines the core traits, types, and builders used throughout the framework.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `macro`- `evento-macro`
- `group`- `EventoGroup`
- `rw`- `Rw`
- `sqlite`- `mysql`- `postgres`
- `fjall`

[§](https://docs.rs#core-concepts)Core Concepts

[§](https://docs.rs#events)Events

Events are immutable facts that represent something that happened in your domain.
The [ Event](https://docs.rs/struct.Event.html) struct stores serialized event data with metadata:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Define events using the aggregate macro
#[evento::aggregate]
pub enum BankAccount {
    AccountOpened { owner_id: String, initial_balance: i64 },
    MoneyDeposited { amount: i64 },
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#executor)Executor

The [ Executor](https://docs.rs/trait.Executor.html) trait abstracts event storage and retrieval. Implementations
handle persisting events, querying, and managing subscriptions.

[§](https://docs.rs#aggregate-builder)Aggregate Builder

Use [ create()](https://docs.rs/fn.create.html) or

[to build and commit events:](https://docs.rs/fn.append.html)

`append()`[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use evento::metadata::Metadata;
let id = evento::create()
    .event(&AccountOpened { owner_id: "user1".into(), initial_balance: 1000 })
    .metadata(&Metadata::default())
    .commit(&executor)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#projections)Projections

Build read models by replaying events. Use the [ projection](https://docs.rs/projection/index.html) module for loading
aggregate state:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use evento::projection::Projection;
#[evento::projection]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AccountView {
    pub balance: i64,
}
#[evento::handler]
async fn on_deposited(
    event: Event<MoneyDeposited>,
    projection: &mut AccountView,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    projection.balance += event.data.amount;
    Ok(())
}
let result = Projection::<_, AccountView>::new::<BankAccount>()
    .handler(on_deposited())
    .load("account-123")
    .execute(&executor)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#subscriptions)Subscriptions

Process events continuously in real-time. See the [ subscription](https://docs.rs/subscription/index.html) module:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use evento::subscription::SubscriptionBuilder;
#[evento::subscription]
async fn on_deposited<E: Executor>(
    context: &Context<'_, E>,
    event: Event<MoneyDeposited>,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // Perform side effects
    Ok(())
}
let subscription = SubscriptionBuilder::<Sqlite>::new("deposit-processor")
    .handler(on_deposited())
    .routing_key("accounts")
    .start(&executor)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#cursor-based-pagination)Cursor-based Pagination

GraphQL-style pagination for querying events. See the [ cursor](https://docs.rs/cursor/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

- `context`
- `cursor`
- `metadata`
- `projection`
- `subscription`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use evento::{Executor, metadata::Metadata, cursor::Args, EventFilter};
// Create and persist an event
let id = evento::create()
    .event(&AccountOpened { owner_id: "user1".into(), initial_balance: 1000 })
    .metadata(&Metadata::default())
    .commit(&executor)
    .await?;
// Query events with pagination
let events = executor.read(
    Some(vec![EventFilter::by_id("myapp/Account", &id)]),
    None,
    Args::forward(10, None),
).await?;
```

# rship_sync - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/

## Expand description

Sync Value System

High-precision synchronized value distribution using hyphae cells. Runs in-process with a 240Hz master clock for value updates.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rship_sync::{context, ValueRunnerRegistry, SyncValueConfig};
use std::sync::Arc;
// Initialize (once at startup)
let registry = Arc::new(ValueRunnerRegistry::new());
context::init(registry);
// Create and watch values
rship_sync::ensure_value("my/value", &SyncValueConfig { value: 0.0, rate: 1.0, running: true }, 30.0);
let cell = rship_sync::watch_value("my/value");
```

# rship_shared_schemas - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-shared-schemas/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_shared_schemas/

## Expand description

Shared schema registry.

Hosts the `WellKnownSchema` enum (a closed set of schemas every SDK knows
about) and the `SchemaRef` reference type used by `Action`, `Emitter`, and
comp-engine entities. Generated to every SDK via typegen so misspelled or
invented schema ids are unrepresentable at compile time.

See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-comp-engine-design.md`
§ “Shared-Schemas Registry”.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use registry::`- [GetSchemaByVariant](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.GetSchemaByVariant.html);
- `pub use registry::`- [GetSchemaByVariantOutput](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.GetSchemaByVariantOutput.html);
- `pub use schema_ref::`- [SchemaRef](https://docs.rs/schema_ref/enum.SchemaRef.html);
- `pub use well_known::`- [SchemaEntry](https://docs.rs/well_known/struct.SchemaEntry.html);
- `pub use well_known::`- [SchemaSemantic](https://docs.rs/well_known/enum.SchemaSemantic.html);
- `pub use well_known::`- [WellKnownSchema](https://docs.rs/well_known/enum.WellKnownSchema.html);
- `pub use well_known::`- [schema_for](https://docs.rs/well_known/fn.schema_for.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [registry](https://docs.rs/registry/index.html)
- Server-side reports for inspecting the shared-schemas registry from the UI.
- [schema_](https://docs.rs/schema_ref/index.html)- ref
- Typed schema-reference enum used by Action, Emitter, and downstream
entities. Prefer `SchemaRef::WellKnown(...)`at call sites; reach for`SchemaRef::Custom(...)`only when no well-known schema fits the value.
- [well_](https://docs.rs/well_known/index.html)- known
- Well-known schema enum — the closed set of schemas rship core knows about.
Every variant has exactly one registered body. Adding a variant requires
extending the exhaustive match in `schema_for`; missing a variant fails to compile.

- Touch this from `typegen`and other binaries to force the linker to keep the`inventory::submit!`registrations alive.

# smooth_operator_adapter_dynamodb - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-adapter-dynamodb/1.11.1/smooth_operator_adapter_dynamodb/

## Expand description

DynamoDB single-table [ StorageAdapter](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/adapter/trait.StorageAdapter.html) — the AWS-serverless backend.

This is the production DynamoDB implementation of the one storage seam (see
`docs/STORAGE.md`). One table, overloaded `PK`/`SK` + two GSIs serve every
access pattern (the keys live in [`keys`]):

- **OLTP**(conversations / participants / messages / sessions): async CRUD over- `aws-sdk-dynamodb`, with the- **same observable semantics**as the in-memory / Postgres baselines — conversation idempotency on- `(org, idempotencyKey)`via a conditional GSI item, external-id participant resolve via- `GSI1`, monotonic message sequencing (an atomic counter item) with cursor paging, session status/counts.
- **Checkpoints**:- `DynamoCheckpointStore`- `CheckpointStore`- `checkpoint`]).
- **Knowledge**:- `DynamoKnowledgeBase`- `s3-vectors`feature (see [- `knowledge`] / [- `s3vectors`]).

[§](https://docs.rs#single-table-key-design)Single-table key design

| Entity | PK | SK | GSI1PK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conversation | `ORG#<org>` | `CONV#<convId>` | `IDEM#<org>#<key>`+`CONV#<id>` |
| Participant | `CONV#<convId>` | `PART#<partId>` | `EXTERNAL#<convId>#<extId>` |
| Message | `CONV#<convId>` | `MSG#<padded seq>#<id>` | `MSG#<id>` |
| Session | `CONV#<convId>` | `SESS#<sessionId>` | `SESSION#<sessionId>` |
| Checkpoint | `CKPT#<agentId>` | `<padded iteration>#<id>` | `CKPTID#<id>` |
| Knowledge | `KNOW#<org>` | `DOC#<docId>` | — |

Each conversation writes **two** GSI1 entries (one by-idempotency, one
by-id), so both `create_conversation` idempotency lookups and standalone
`get_conversation(id)` are single queries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Deterministic](https://docs.rs/struct.DeterministicEmbedder.html)- Embedder
- Deterministic, network-free pseudo-embedder.
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoCheckpointStore.html)- Checkpoint - Store
- DynamoDB-backed checkpoint store. Cheap to clone (a `Client`+`Handle`+ table name behind`Arc`-able fields).
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoConnectorConfigStore.html)- Connector - Config - Store
- DynamoDB-backed `ConnectorConfigStore`
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoDbAdapter.html)- DbAdapter
- DynamoDB single-table storage adapter.
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoIndexingStore.html)- Indexing - Store
- DynamoDB-backed `IndexingStore`
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoKnowledgeBase.html)- Knowledge - Base
- DynamoDB-backed knowledge base. Cheap to clone.
- [Dynamo](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamoSettingsStore.html)- Settings - Store
- DynamoDB-backed `SettingsStore`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.InputType.html)- Type
- Whether an embedding is for a document being stored or a search query.
- [Knowledge](https://docs.rs/enum.KnowledgeBackend.html)- Backend
- Which dense-retrieval backend the knowledge slice uses.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIM.html)- EMBEDDING_ - DIM
- Default embedding dimension (Voyage `voyage-3-large`shape; mirrors smooai’s`knowledge_vectors embedding vector(1024)`).
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_TABLE_NAME.html)- TABLE_ - NAME
- Default table name when none is configured.
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_INLINE_BLOB.html)- INLINE_ - BLOB
- Conservative inline-blob ceiling. DynamoDB’s hard item limit is 400 KB; we
trip earlier (~300 KB) to leave headroom for keys/metadata and to fail loud
*before*the SDK rejects the`PutItem`. Blobs above this must spill to S3.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Embedder](https://docs.rs/trait.Embedder.html)
- Turn text into dense vectors. Implementations must return one vector per
input string, each of length `Embedder::dim`

# scale-info 2.11.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/scale-info/2.11.6

A library to describe Rust types, geared towards providing info about the structure of [SCALE
](https://github.com/paritytech/parity-scale-codec) encodable types.

The definitions provide third party tools (e.g. a UI client) with information about how they are able to decode types agnostic of language.

At its core is the `TypeInfo` trait:

```
```
Types implementing this trait build up and return a `Type` struct:

```
```
Types are defined as one of the following variants:

```
```
## Built-in Type Definitions

The following "built-in" types have predefined `TypeInfo` definitions:

-
**Primitives:**`bool`,`char`,`str`,`u8`,`u16`,`u32`,`u64`,`u128`,`i8`,`i16`,`i32`,`i64`,`i128`.
-
**Sequence:**Variable size sequence of elements of`T`, where`T`implements`TypeInfo`. e.g.`[T]`,`&[T]`,`&mut [T]`,`Vec<T>`
-
**Array:**Fixed size`[T: $n]`for any`T`which implements`TypeInfo`, where`$n`is one of the predefined sizes.
-
**Tuple:**Tuples consisting of up to 10 fields with types implementing`TypeInfo`.

## User-defined Types

There are two kinds of user-defined types: `Composite` and `Variant`.

Both make use of the `Path` and `Field` types in their definition:

### Fields

A fundamental building block to represent user defined types is the `Field` struct which defines the `Type` of a
field together with its optional name. Builders for the user defined types enforce the invariant that either all
fields have a name (e.g. structs) or all fields are unnamed (e.g. tuples).

### Path

The path of a type is a unique sequence of identifiers. Rust types typically construct a path from
the namespace and the identifier e.g. `foo::bar::Baz` is converted to the path `["foo", "bar",  "Baz"]`.

### Composite

[Composite data types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_data_type) are composed of a set of `Fields`.

**Structs** are represented by a set of *named* fields, enforced during construction:

```
```
**Tuples** are represented by a set of *unnamed* fields, enforced during construction:

```
;
```
### Variant

[Variant types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagged_union) aka enums or tagged unions are
composed of a set of variants. Variants can have unnamed fields, named fields or no fields at all:

```
```
If no variants contain fields then the discriminant can be set explicitly, enforced by the builder during construction:

```
```
## The Registry

Information about types is provided within the so-called type registry (`Registry`).
Type definitions are registered there and are associated with unique IDs that the outside
can refer to, providing a lightweight way to decrease overhead instead of using type
identifiers.

All concrete `TypeInfo` structures have two forms:

- One meta form (`MetaType`) that acts as a bridge to other forms
- A portable form suitable for serialization.

The `IntoPortable` trait must also be implemented in order prepare a type
definition for serialization using an instance of the type registry.

After transformation all type definitions are stored in the type registry. Note that the type registry should be serialized as part of the metadata structure where the registered types are utilized to allow consumers to resolve the types.

## Encoding

The type registry can be encoded as:

- JSON (with the "serde" feature enabled).
- SCALE itself (using `parity-scale-codec`).

## Features

The following optional `cargo` features are available:

- **serde**includes support for json serialization/deserialization of the type registry. See example- [here](https://github.com/paritytech/scale-info/blob/master/test_suite/tests/json.rs).
- **derive**reexports the- `scale-info-derive`

## Known issues

When deriving `TypeInfo` for a type with generic compact fields e.g.

```
```
You may experience the following error when using this generic type without the correct bounds:

```
```
See [https://github.com/paritytech/scale-info/issues/65](https://github.com/paritytech/scale-info/issues/65) for more information.

## Resources

- See usage for describing types for `ink!`
- [Original design draft (](https://hackmd.io/0wWm0ueBSF26m2pBG5NaeQ?view)- *outdated*)

# scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/scale-info/2.11.6/target-redirect/scale_info/

## Expand description

Efficient and space-efficient serialization of Rust types.

This library provides structures to easily retrieve compile-time type
information at runtime and also to serialize this information in a
space-efficient form, aka `PortableForm`.

[§](https://docs.rs#registry)Registry

At the heart of its functionality is the [ Registry](https://docs.rs/struct.Registry.html)
that acts as a cache for known types in order to efficiently deduplicate
types and ensure a space-efficient serialization.

[§](https://docs.rs#type-information)Type Information

Information about types is provided via the [ TypeInfo](https://docs.rs/trait.TypeInfo.html)
trait.

This trait should be implemented for all types that are serializable.
`scale-info` provides implementations for all commonly used Rust standard
types and a derive macro for implementing of custom types.

[§](https://docs.rs#deriving-typeinfo)Deriving `TypeInfo`

Enable the `derive` feature of this crate:

`scale-info = { version = "2.0.0", features = ["derive"] }`[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use scale_info::TypeInfo;
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
struct MyStruct {
    a: u32,
    b: MyEnum,
}
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
enum MyEnum {
    A(bool),
    B { f: Vec<u8> },
    C,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)Attributes

[§](https://docs.rs#scale_infobounds)`#[scale_info(bounds(..))]`

Replace the auto-generated `where` clause bounds for the derived `TypeInfo` implementation.

The derive macro automatically adds `TypeInfo` bounds for all type parameters, and all field
types containing type parameters or associated types.

This is naive and sometimes adds unnecessary bounds, since on a syntactical level there is no way to differentiate between a generic type constructor and a type alias with a generic argument e.g.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
trait MyTrait {
    type A;
}
type MyAlias<T> = <T as MyTrait>::A;
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
struct MyStruct<T> {
    a: MyAlias<T>,
    b: Vec<T>,
}
```
So for the above, since a `MyAlias<T>: TypeInfo` bound is required, and we can’t distinguish
between `MyAlias<T>` and `Vec<T>`, then the `TypeInfo` bound is simply added for all
fields which contain any type param. In this case the redundant `Vec<T>: TypeInfo`
would be added.

This is usually okay, but in some circumstances can cause problems, for example with the
[`overflow evaluating the requirement`] error [here](https://github.com/paritytech/scale-info/blob/master/test_suite/tests/ui/pass_custom_bounds_fix_overflow.rs).

The `bounds` attribute provides an [“escape hatch”](https://serde.rs/attr-bound.html) to allow
the programmer control of the `where` clause on the generated `impl`, to solve this and other
issues that can’t be foreseen by the auto-generated bounds heuristic.

[§](https://docs.rs#scale_infoskip_type_params)`#[scale_info(skip_type_params(..))]`

Remove the requirement for the specified type params to implement `TypeInfo`.

Consider a simple example of a type parameter which is used for associated types, but the type itself does not carry any type information. Consider this common pattern:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
trait Config {
    type Balance;
}
struct Runtime; // doesn't implement `TypeInfo`
impl Config for Runtime {
    type Balance = u64;
}
#[allow(unused)]
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
#[scale_info(skip_type_params(T))]
struct A<T: Config> {
    balance: T::Balance,
    marker: core::marker::PhantomData<T>,
}
fn assert_type_info<T: scale_info::TypeInfo + 'static>() {}
fn main() {
    // without the `skip_type_params` attribute this will fail.
    assert_type_info::<A<Runtime>>();
}
```
By default, the derived `TypeInfo` implementation will add the type of all type parameters to
the `TypeParameter` specification e.g.

`type_params(vec![TypeParameter::new("T", Some(MetaType::new::<T>()))])`

In the example above, this will cause a compiler error because `Runtime` is the concrete tyoe
for `T`, which does not satisfy the `TypeInfo` requirement of `MetaType::new::<T>()`.

Simply adding a `TypeInfo` derive to `Runtime` is one way of solving this, but that could be
misleading (why does it need `TypeInfo` if a value of that type is never encoded?), and can
sometimes require adding `TypeInfo` bounds in other impl blocks.

The `skip_type_params` attribute solves this, providing an additional “escape hatch” which
prevents the given type parameter’s type information being required:

`type_params(vec![TypeParameter::new("T", None)])`

The generated type params do not now require `T` to implement `TypeInfo`, so the auto-generated
bound is not added to the generated `TypeInfo` `where` clause.

[§](https://docs.rs#combining-bounds-and-skip_type_params)Combining `bounds` and `skip_type_params`

These two attributes can complement one another, particularly in the case where using `bounds`
would still require manually adding a `TypeInfo` bound for the type parameter:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
#[scale_info(bounds(), skip_type_params(T))]
struct A<T> {
    marker: core::marker::PhantomData<T>,
}
```
Without `skip_type_params` in the example above, it would require the `TypeInfo` bounds for `T`
to be added manually e.g. `#[scale_info(bounds(T: TypeInfo + 'static))]`. Since the intention of
the empty bounds is to **remove** all type bounds, then the addition of `skip_type_params`
allows this to compile successfully.

[§](https://docs.rs#precedence)Precedence

When used independently, both attributes modify the `where` clause of the derived `TypeInfo`
impl. When used together, the predicates supplied in the `bounds` attribute replaces *all*
auto-generated bounds, and `skip_type_params` will have no effect on the resulting `where`
clause.

**Note:** When using `bounds` without `skip_type_params`, it is therefore required to manually
add a `TypeInfo` bound for any non skipped type parameters. The compiler will let you know.

[§](https://docs.rs#scale_infocapture_docs--defaultalwaysnever)`#[scale_info(capture_docs = "default|always|never")]`

Docs for types, fields and variants can all be captured by the `docs` feature being enabled.
This can be overridden using the `capture_docs` attribute:

`#[scale_info(capture_docs = "default")]` will capture docs iff the `docs` feature is enabled.
This is the default if `capture_docs` is not specified.

`#[scale_info(capture_docs = "always")]` will capture docs for the annotated type even if the
`docs` feature is *not* enabled.

`#[scale_info(capture_docs = "never")]` will *not* capture docs for the annotated type even if
the `docs` is enabled.

This is useful e.g. when compiling metadata into a Wasm blob, and it is desirable to keep the
binary size as small as possible, so the `docs` feature would be disabled. In case the docs for
some types is necessary they could be enabled on a per-type basis with the above attribute.

[§](https://docs.rs#scale_infocrate--pathtocrate)`#[scale_info(crate = path::to::crate)]`

Specify a path to the scale-info crate instance to use when referring to the APIs from generated code. This is normally only applicable when invoking re-exported scale-info derives from a public macro in a different crate. For example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use scale_info_reexport::info::TypeInfo;
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
#[scale_info(crate = scale_info_reexport::info)]
enum TestEnum {
    FirstVariant,
    SecondVariant,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#scale_inforeplace_segmentsearch-replace)`#[scale_info(replace_segment("search", "replace"))]`

Specify to rename a segment in the `path` returned by the [`TypeInfo::path`] function.
Normally the path is generated by using the `module_path!` macro. This path includes
the crate name and all the modules up to the declaration of the type. Sometimes it
is useful to replace one of these segments to ensure that for example a renaming
of the crate isn’t propagated to downstream users. Be aware that if a `crate-name`
contains an hypen, the actual segment is `crate_name`. The `replace` name needs
to be a valid Rust identifier. The attribute is allowed to be passed multiple
times to replace multiple segments.

Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use scale_info_reexport::info::TypeInfo;
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
#[scale_info(replace_segment("something", "better_name"))]
#[scale_info(replace_segment("TestEnum", "BetterEnumName"))]
enum TestEnum {
    FirstVariant,
    SecondVariant,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#forms)Forms

To bridge between compile-time type information and runtime the
[ MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html) is used to easily retrieve all
information needed to uniquely identify types.

The `MetaForm` and its associated `Registry` can be transformed into the
space-efficient form by the [ IntoPortable](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoPortable.html) trait; it is
used internally by the

[in order to convert the expanded types into their space-efficient form.](https://docs.rs/struct.Registry.html)

`Registry`[§](https://docs.rs#symbols-and-namespaces)Symbols and Namespaces

To differentiate two types sharing the same name, namespaces are used.
Commonly the namespace is equal to the one where the type has been defined
in. For Rust prelude types such as [ Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html) and

[the root namespace (empty namespace) is used.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`To use this library simply use the [ MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html)
initially with your own data structures; make them generic over the

[trait just as has been done in this crate with](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html)

`Form`[in order to get a simple implementation of](https://docs.rs/trait.TypeInfo.html)

`TypeInfo`[. Use a single instance of the](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoPortable.html)

`IntoPortable`[for compaction and provide this registry instance upon serialization.](https://docs.rs/struct.Registry.html)

`Registry`A usage example can be found in ink! here: https://github.com/paritytech/ink/blob/master/abi/src/specs.rs

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [build](https://docs.rs/build/index.html)

- [form](https://docs.rs/form/index.html)

}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#scale_inforeplace_segmentsearch-replace)`#[scale_info(replace_segment("search", "replace"))]`

Specify to rename a segment in the `path` returned by the [`TypeInfo::path`] function.
Normally the path is generated by using the `module_path!` macro. This path includes
the crate name and all the modules up to the declaration of the type. Sometimes it
is useful to replace one of these segments to ensure that for example a renaming
of the crate isn’t propagated to downstream users. Be aware that if a `crate-name`
contains an hypen, the actual segment is `crate_name`. The `replace` name needs
to be a valid Rust identifier. The attribute is allowed to be passed multiple
times to replace multiple segments.

Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use scale_info_reexport::info::TypeInfo;
#[derive(TypeInfo)]
#[scale_info(replace_segment("something", "better_name"))]
#[scale_info(replace_segment("TestEnum", "BetterEnumName"))]
enum TestEnum {
    FirstVariant,
    SecondVariant,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#forms)Forms

To bridge between compile-time type information and runtime the
[ MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html) is used to easily retrieve all
information needed to uniquely identify types.

The `MetaForm` and its associated `Registry` can be transformed into the
space-efficient form by the [ IntoPortable](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoPortable.html) trait; it is
used internally by the

[in order to convert the expanded types into their space-efficient form.](https://docs.rs/struct.Registry.html)

`Registry`[§](https://docs.rs#symbols-and-namespaces)Symbols and Namespaces

To differentiate two types sharing the same name, namespaces are used.
Commonly the namespace is equal to the one where the type has been defined
in. For Rust prelude types such as [ Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html) and

[the root namespace (empty namespace) is used.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`To use this library simply use the [ MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html)
initially with your own data structures; make them generic over the

[trait just as has been done in this crate with](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html)

`Form`[in order to get a simple implementation of](https://docs.rs/trait.TypeInfo.html)

`TypeInfo`[. Use a single instance of the](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoPortable.html)

`IntoPortable`[for compaction and provide this registry instance upon serialization.](https://docs.rs/struct.Registry.html)

`Registry`A usage example can be found in ink! here: https://github.com/paritytech/ink/blob/master/abi/src/specs.rs

# scale_info/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// Copyright 2019-2022 Parity Technologies (UK) Ltd.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//
[3](https://docs.rs#3)// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");

[5](https://docs.rs#5)// You may obtain a copy of the License at
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//
[9](https://docs.rs#9)// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
[10](https://docs.rs#10)// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
[11](https://docs.rs#11)// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
[13](https://docs.rs#13)// limitations under the License.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)
[15](https://docs.rs#15)#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]
[16](https://docs.rs#16)#![deny(missing_docs)]
[17](https://docs.rs#17)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! Efficient and space-efficient serialization of Rust types.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! This library provides structures to easily retrieve compile-time type
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! information at runtime and also to serialize this information in a
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! space-efficient form, aka `PortableForm`.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! # Registry
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! At the heart of its functionality is the [`Registry`](`crate::Registry`)
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! that acts as a cache for known types in order to efficiently deduplicate
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! types and ensure a space-efficient serialization.
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! # Type Information
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! Information about types is provided via the [`TypeInfo`](`crate::TypeInfo`)
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! trait.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! This trait should be implemented for all types that are serializable.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! `scale-info` provides implementations for all commonly used Rust standard
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! types and a derive macro for implementing of custom types.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! ## Deriving `TypeInfo`
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! Enable the `derive` feature of this crate:
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! ```toml
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! scale-info = { version = "2.0.0", features = ["derive"] }
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! ```
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! ```ignore
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! use scale_info::TypeInfo;
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! struct MyStruct {
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!     a: u32,
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!     b: MyEnum,
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! }
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! enum MyEnum {
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!     A(bool),
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!     B { f: Vec<u8> },
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!     C,
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! }
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! ```
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! ### Attributes
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! #### `#[scale_info(bounds(..))]`
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! Replace the auto-generated `where` clause bounds for the derived `TypeInfo` implementation.
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! ```ignore
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! #[scale_info(bounds(T: TypeInfo + 'static))]
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! struct MyStruct<T> {
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!     a: Vec<T>,
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! }
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! ```
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! The derive macro automatically adds `TypeInfo` bounds for all type parameters, and all field
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! types containing type parameters or associated types.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! This is naive and sometimes adds unnecessary bounds, since on a syntactical level there is no
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! way to differentiate between a generic type constructor and a type alias with a generic argument
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! e.g.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! ```ignore
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! trait MyTrait {
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!     type A;
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! }
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! type MyAlias<T> = <T as MyTrait>::A;
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! struct MyStruct<T> {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     a: MyAlias<T>,
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!     b: Vec<T>,
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! }
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! ```
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! So for the above, since a `MyAlias<T>: TypeInfo` bound is required, and we can't distinguish
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! between `MyAlias<T>` and `Vec<T>`, then the `TypeInfo` bound is simply added for all
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! fields which contain any type param. In this case the redundant `Vec<T>: TypeInfo`
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! would be added.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! This is usually okay, but in some circumstances can cause problems, for example with the
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! [`overflow evaluating the requirement`] error [here](https://github.com/paritytech/scale-info/blob/master/test_suite/tests/ui/pass_custom_bounds_fix_overflow.rs).
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! The `bounds` attribute provides an ["escape hatch"](https://serde.rs/attr-bound.html) to allow
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! the programmer control of the `where` clause on the generated `impl`, to solve this and other
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! issues that can't be foreseen by the auto-generated bounds heuristic.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! #### `#[scale_info(skip_type_params(..))]`
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//!
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! Remove the requirement for the specified type params to implement `TypeInfo`.
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! Consider a simple example of a type parameter which is used for associated types, but the type
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! itself does not carry any type information. Consider this common pattern:
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//!
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! ```ignore
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! trait Config {
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!     type Balance;
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! }
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! struct Runtime; // doesn't implement `TypeInfo`
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! impl Config for Runtime {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!     type Balance = u64;
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//! }
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! #[allow(unused)]
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//! #[scale_info(skip_type_params(T))]
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! struct A<T: Config> {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!     balance: T::Balance,
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!     marker: core::marker::PhantomData<T>,
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! }
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! fn assert_type_info<T: scale_info::TypeInfo + 'static>() {}
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! fn main() {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!     // without the `skip_type_params` attribute this will fail.
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     assert_type_info::<A<Runtime>>();
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//! }
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! ```
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//! By default, the derived `TypeInfo` implementation will add the type of all type parameters to
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! the `TypeParameter` specification e.g.
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! `type_params(vec![TypeParameter::new("T", Some(MetaType::new::<T>()))])`
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! In the example above, this will cause a compiler error because `Runtime` is the concrete tyoe
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//! for `T`, which does not satisfy the `TypeInfo` requirement of `MetaType::new::<T>()`.
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! Simply adding a `TypeInfo` derive to `Runtime` is one way of solving this, but that could be
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! misleading (why does it need `TypeInfo` if a value of that type is never encoded?), and can
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! sometimes require adding `TypeInfo` bounds in other impl blocks.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//!
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! The `skip_type_params` attribute solves this, providing an additional "escape hatch" which
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! prevents the given type parameter's type information being required:
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! `type_params(vec![TypeParameter::new("T", None)])`
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//! The generated type params do not now require `T` to implement `TypeInfo`, so the auto-generated
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! bound is not added to the generated `TypeInfo` `where` clause.
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//! #### Combining `bounds` and `skip_type_params`
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! These two attributes can complement one another, particularly in the case where using `bounds`
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! would still require manually adding a `TypeInfo` bound for the type parameter:
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! ```ignore
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! #[scale_info(bounds(), skip_type_params(T))]
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! struct A<T> {
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!     marker: core::marker::PhantomData<T>,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! }
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! ```
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//!
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! Without `skip_type_params` in the example above, it would require the `TypeInfo` bounds for `T`
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! to be added manually e.g. `#[scale_info(bounds(T: TypeInfo + 'static))]`. Since the intention of
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! the empty bounds is to **remove** all type bounds, then the addition of `skip_type_params`
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! allows this to compile successfully.
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! ##### Precedence
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! When used independently, both attributes modify the `where` clause of the derived `TypeInfo`
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! impl. When used together, the predicates supplied in the `bounds` attribute replaces *all*
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! auto-generated bounds, and `skip_type_params` will have no effect on the resulting `where`
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! clause.
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! **Note:** When using `bounds` without `skip_type_params`, it is therefore required to manually
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! add a `TypeInfo` bound for any non skipped type parameters. The compiler will let you know.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//!
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! #### `#[scale_info(capture_docs = "default|always|never")]`
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//!
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! Docs for types, fields and variants can all be captured by the `docs` feature being enabled.
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! This can be overridden using the `capture_docs` attribute:
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//!
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! `#[scale_info(capture_docs = "default")]` will capture docs iff the `docs` feature is enabled.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! This is the default if `capture_docs` is not specified.
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! `#[scale_info(capture_docs = "always")]` will capture docs for the annotated type even if the
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//! `docs` feature is *not* enabled.
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//!
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! `#[scale_info(capture_docs = "never")]` will *not* capture docs for the annotated type even if
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//! the `docs` is enabled.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//!
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//! This is useful e.g. when compiling metadata into a Wasm blob, and it is desirable to keep the
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//! binary size as small as possible, so the `docs` feature would be disabled. In case the docs for
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//! some types is necessary they could be enabled on a per-type basis with the above attribute.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! #### `#[scale_info(crate = path::to::crate)]`
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! Specify a path to the scale-info crate instance to use when referring to the APIs from generated
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//! code. This is normally only applicable when invoking re-exported scale-info derives from a public
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! macro in a different crate. For example:
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! ```ignore
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! use scale_info_reexport::info::TypeInfo;
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! #[scale_info(crate = scale_info_reexport::info)]
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! enum TestEnum {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!     FirstVariant,
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//!     SecondVariant,
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//! }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! ```
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! #### `#[scale_info(replace_segment("search", "replace"))]`
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//!
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//! Specify to rename a segment in the `path` returned by the [`TypeInfo::path`] function.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! Normally the path is generated by using the `module_path!` macro. This path includes
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! the crate name and all the modules up to the declaration of the type. Sometimes it
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//! is useful to replace one of these segments to ensure that for example a renaming
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//! of the crate isn't propagated to downstream users. Be aware that if a `crate-name`
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//! contains an hypen, the actual segment is `crate_name`. The `replace` name needs
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//! to be a valid Rust identifier. The attribute is allowed to be passed multiple
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//! times to replace multiple segments.
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//!
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//! Example:
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! ```ignore
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! use scale_info_reexport::info::TypeInfo;
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//! #[derive(TypeInfo)]
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//! #[scale_info(replace_segment("something", "better_name"))]
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//! #[scale_info(replace_segment("TestEnum", "BetterEnumName"))]
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//! enum TestEnum {
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!     FirstVariant,
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!     SecondVariant,
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//! ```
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//!
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//! # Forms
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//!
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//! To bridge between compile-time type information and runtime the
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//! [`MetaForm`](`crate::form::MetaForm`) is used to easily retrieve all
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! information needed to uniquely identify types.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//!
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//! The `MetaForm` and its associated `Registry` can be transformed into the
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//! space-efficient form by the [`IntoPortable`](`crate::IntoPortable`) trait; it is
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! used internally by the [`Registry`](`crate::Registry`) in order to convert
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! the expanded types into their space-efficient form.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//! # Symbols and Namespaces
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//!
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//! To differentiate two types sharing the same name, namespaces are used.
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//! Commonly the namespace is equal to the one where the type has been defined
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//! in. For Rust prelude types such as [`Option`](`std::option::Option`) and
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//! [`Result`](`std::result::Result`) the root namespace (empty namespace) is
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//! used.
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//!
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//! To use this library simply use the [`MetaForm`](`crate::form::MetaForm`)
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//! initially with your own data structures; make them generic over the
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//! [`Form`](`crate::form::Form`) trait just as has been done in this crate with
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//! [`TypeInfo`](`crate::TypeInfo`) in order to get a simple implementation of
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//! [`IntoPortable`](`crate::IntoPortable`). Use a single instance of the
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//! [`Registry`](`crate::Registry`) for compaction and provide this registry
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//! instance upon serialization.
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//!
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//! A usage example can be found in ink! here:
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//! https://github.com/paritytech/ink/blob/master/abi/src/specs.rs
[280](https://docs.rs#280)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// Takes a number of types and returns a vector that contains their respective
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// [`MetaType`](`crate::MetaType`) instances.
[283](https://docs.rs#283)///
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// This is useful for places that require inputs of iterators over [`MetaType`](`crate::MetaType`)
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// instances and provide a way out of code bloat in these scenarios.
[286](https://docs.rs#286)///
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// # Example
[288](https://docs.rs#288)///
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// ```
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// # use scale_info::tuple_meta_type;
[291](https://docs.rs#291)/// assert_eq!(
[292](https://docs.rs#292)///     tuple_meta_type!(i32, [u8; 32], String),
[293](https://docs.rs#293)///     {
[294](https://docs.rs#294)///         use scale_info::MetaType;
[295](https://docs.rs#295)///         let mut vec = Vec::new();
[296](https://docs.rs#296)///         vec.push(MetaType::new::<i32>());
[297](https://docs.rs#297)///         vec.push(MetaType::new::<[u8; 32]>());
[298](https://docs.rs#298)///         vec.push(MetaType::new::<String>());
[299](https://docs.rs#299)///         vec
[300](https://docs.rs#300)///     }
[301](https://docs.rs#301)/// );
[302](https://docs.rs#302)/// ```
[303](https://docs.rs#303)#[macro_export]
[304](https://docs.rs#304)macro_rules! tuple_meta_type {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    ( $($ty:ty),* ) => {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        {
[307](https://docs.rs#307)            $crate::prelude::vec![
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                $(
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                    $crate::MetaType::new::<$ty>(),
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                )*
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            ]
[312](https://docs.rs#312)        }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    }
[314](https://docs.rs#314)}
[315](https://docs.rs#315)
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// Construct a vector of `TypeParameter`s from pairs of the name and the concrete type.
[317](https://docs.rs#317)///
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// # Example
[319](https://docs.rs#319)///
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// ```
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// # use scale_info::{named_type_params, MetaType, TypeParameter};
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// assert_eq!(
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///     named_type_params![(T, u8), (U, u32)],
[324](https://docs.rs#324)///     vec! [
[325](https://docs.rs#325)///         TypeParameter::new("T", Some(MetaType::new::<u8>())),
[326](https://docs.rs#326)///         TypeParameter::new("U", Some(MetaType::new::<u32>())),
[327](https://docs.rs#327)///     ]
[328](https://docs.rs#328)/// );
[329](https://docs.rs#329)/// ```
[330](https://docs.rs#330)#[macro_export]
[331](https://docs.rs#331)macro_rules! named_type_params {
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    ( $(($tp:ty, $ty:ty)),* ) => {
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        {
[334](https://docs.rs#334)            $crate::prelude::vec![
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                $(
[336](https://docs.rs#336)                    $crate::TypeParameter::<$crate::form::MetaForm>::new(
[337](https://docs.rs#337)                        ::core::stringify!($tp),
[338](https://docs.rs#338)                        Some($crate::MetaType::new::<$ty>())
[339](https://docs.rs#339)                    ),
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                )*
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            ]
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        }
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    }
[344](https://docs.rs#344)}
[345](https://docs.rs#345)
[346](https://docs.rs#346)/// Construct a vector of [`TypeParameter`] instances with the name of the type parameter,
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// together with its concrete [`MetaType`].
[348](https://docs.rs#348)#[macro_export]
[349](https://docs.rs#349)macro_rules! type_params {
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    ( $($ty:ty),* ) => {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)        $crate::named_type_params!{ $( ($ty, $ty) ),* }
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    }
[353](https://docs.rs#353)}

# Registry in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.Registry.html

`pub struct Registry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The registry for space-efficient storage of type identifiers and definitions.

The registry consists of a cache for type identifiers and definitions.

When adding a type to the registry, all of its sub-types are registered recursively as well. A type is considered a sub-type of another type if it is used by its identifier or structure.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

A type can be a sub-type of itself. In this case the registry has a builtin mechanism to stop recursion and avoid going into an infinite loop.

#### pub fn [register_type](https://docs.rs#method.register_type)(&mut self, ty: &[MetaType](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaType.html)) -> [UntrackedSymbol](https://docs.rs/interner/struct.UntrackedSymbol.html)<[TypeId](https://docs.rs/prelude/any/struct.TypeId.html)>

Registers the given type into the registry and returns its associated type ID symbol.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-1)Note

Due to safety requirements the returns type ID symbol cannot be used later to resolve back to the associated type definition. However, since this facility is going to be used for serialization purposes this functionality isn’t needed anyway.

# TypeInfo in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/trait.TypeInfo.html

## Expand description

Implementors return their meta type information.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

The type identifying for which type info is provided.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

This is used to uniquely identify a type via [ core::any::TypeId::of](https://docs.rs/prelude/any/struct.TypeId.html#method.of). In most cases it
will just be

`Self`, but can be used to unify different types which have the same encoded
representation e.g. reference types `Box<T>`, `&T` and `&mut T`.## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

Allows to be converted into other forms such as portable form
through the registry and `IntoPortable`.

This allows for type-level separation between free forms that can be instantiated out of the flux and portable forms that require some sort of interning data structures.

# scale_info::build - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/build/index.html

## Expand description

Builders for defining metadata for variant types (enums), and composite types (structs). They are designed to allow only construction of valid definitions.

In most cases we recommend using the `scale-info-derive` crate to auto generate the builder
constructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-struct)Generic struct

```
struct Foo<T> {
    bar: T,
    data: u64,
}
impl<T> TypeInfo for Foo<T>
where
    T: TypeInfo + 'static,
{
    type Identity = Self;
    fn type_info() -> Type {
        Type::builder()
            .path(Path::new("Foo", module_path!()))
            .type_params(type_params!(T))
            .composite(Fields::named()
                .field(|f| f.ty::<T>().name("bar").type_name("T"))
                .field(|f| f.ty::<u64>().name("data").type_name("u64"))
            )
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tuple-struct)Tuple struct

```
struct Foo(u32, bool);
impl TypeInfo for Foo {
    type Identity = Self;
    fn type_info() -> Type {
        Type::builder()
            .path(Path::new("Foo", module_path!()))
            .composite(Fields::unnamed()
                .field(|f| f.ty::<u32>().type_name("u32"))
                .field(|f| f.ty::<bool>().type_name("bool"))
            )
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#enum-with-fields)Enum with fields

```
enum Foo<T>{
    A(T),
    B { f: u32 },
    C,
}
impl<T> TypeInfo for Foo<T>
where
    T: TypeInfo + 'static,
{
    type Identity = Self;
    fn type_info() -> Type {
        Type::builder()
            .path(Path::new("Foo", module_path!()))
               .type_params(type_params!(T))
            .variant(
                Variants::new()
                    .variant("A", |v| v
                        .index(0)
                        .fields(Fields::unnamed().field(|f| f.ty::<T>().type_name("T")))
                    )
                    .variant("B", |v| v
                        .index(1)
                        .fields(Fields::named().field(|f| f.ty::<u32>().name("f").type_name("u32")))
                    )
                    .variant_unit("A", 2)
            )
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#enum-without-fields-aka-c-style-enums)Enum without fields, aka C-style enums.

```
enum Foo {
    A,
    B,
    C = 33,
}
impl TypeInfo for Foo {
    type Identity = Self;
    fn type_info() -> Type {
        Type::builder()
            .path(Path::new("Foo", module_path!()))
            .variant(
                Variants::new()
                    .variant("A", |v| v.index(1))
                    .variant("B", |v| v.index(2))
                    .variant("C", |v| v.index(33))
            )
    }
}
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [field_](https://docs.rs/field_state/index.html)- state
- Type states for building a field.
- [state](https://docs.rs/state/index.html)
- State types for type builders which require a Path.
- [variant_](https://docs.rs/variant_state/index.html)- state
- State types for the `VariantBuilder`which requires an index.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldBuilder.html)- Builder
- Construct a valid `Field`
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.Fields.html)
- Provides FieldsBuilder constructors
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsBuilder.html)- Builder
- Build a set of either all named (e.g. for a struct) or all unnamed (e.g. for a tuple struct)
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builds a `Type`
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantBuilder.html)- Builder
- Build a `Variant`
- [Variants](https://docs.rs/struct.Variants.html)
- Builds a definition of a variant type i.e an `enum`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Named](https://docs.rs/enum.NamedFields.html)- Fields
- A fields builder only allows named fields (e.g. a struct)
- [NoFields](https://docs.rs/enum.NoFields.html)
- A fields builder has no fields (e.g. a unit struct)
- [Unnamed](https://docs.rs/enum.UnnamedFields.html)- Fields
- A fields builder only allows unnamed fields (e.g. a tuple)

# scale_info::form - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/form/index.html

## Expand description

Provides form definitions.

The forms provided here are used to generically communicate the mode a type identifier, type definition or structure is using.

The default form is the `MetaForm`.
It uses `MetaType` for communicating type identifiers and thus acts as
a bridge from runtime to compile time type information.

The `PortableForm` is a space-efficient representation
that no longer has any connections to the interning registry and thus
can no longer be used to retrieve information from the
original registry. Its sole purpose is for space-efficient serialization.

Other forms, such as a portable form that is still bound to the registry (also via lifetime tracking) are possible but current not needed.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Meta](https://docs.rs/enum.MetaForm.html)- Form
- A meta meta-type.
- [Portable](https://docs.rs/enum.PortableForm.html)- Form
- Portable form that has its lifetime untracked in association to its interner.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Form](https://docs.rs/trait.Form.html)
- Trait to control the internal structures of type definitions.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonSchemaMaybe.html)- Schema - Maybe
- Trait to support derivation of `JsonSchema`for schema generation.

---

# scale_info::interner - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/interner/index.html

## Expand description

Interning data structure and associated symbol definitions.

The interner is used by the registry in order to deduplicate strings and type definitions. Strings are uniquely identified by their contents while types are uniquely identified by their respective type identifiers.

The interners provide a strict ordered sequence of cached (interned) elements and is later used for space-efficient serialization within the registry.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Interner](https://docs.rs/struct.Interner.html)
- Interning data structure generic over the element type.
- [Symbol](https://docs.rs/struct.Symbol.html)
- A symbol from an interner.
- [Untracked](https://docs.rs/struct.UntrackedSymbol.html)- Symbol
- A symbol that is not lifetime tracked.

# named_type_params in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/macro.named_type_params.html

```
macro_rules! named_type_params {
    ( $(($tp:ty, $ty:ty)),* ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Construct a vector of `TypeParameter`s from pairs of the name and the concrete type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
assert_eq!(
    named_type_params![(T, u8), (U, u32)],
    vec! [
        TypeParameter::new("T", Some(MetaType::new::<u8>())),
        TypeParameter::new("U", Some(MetaType::new::<u32>())),
    ]
);
```

# tuple_meta_type in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/macro.tuple_meta_type.html

```
macro_rules! tuple_meta_type {
    ( $($ty:ty),* ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Takes a number of types and returns a vector that contains their respective
[ MetaType](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaType.html) instances.

This is useful for places that require inputs of iterators over [ MetaType](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaType.html)
instances and provide a way out of code bloat in these scenarios.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
assert_eq!(
    tuple_meta_type!(i32, [u8; 32], String),
    {
        use scale_info::MetaType;
        let mut vec = Vec::new();
        vec.push(MetaType::new::<i32>());
        vec.push(MetaType::new::<[u8; 32]>());
        vec.push(MetaType::new::<String>());
        vec
    }
);
```

---

# MetaType in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.MetaType.html

`pub struct MetaType { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A metatype abstraction.

Allows to store compile-time type information at runtime. This again allows to derive type ID and type definition from it.

This needs a conversion to another representation of types in order to be serializable.

# Field in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.Field.html

`pub struct Field<T: `[Form](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html) = [MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html)> {
    pub name: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T::[String](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.String)>,
    pub ty: T::[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type),
    pub type_name: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T::[String](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.String)>,
    pub docs: [Vec](https://docs.rs/prelude/vec/struct.Vec.html)<T::[String](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.String)>,
}## Expand description

A field of a struct-like data type.

Name is optional so it can represent both named and unnamed fields.

This can be a named field of a struct type or an enum struct variant, or an unnamed field of a tuple struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#type-name)Type name

The `type_name` field contains a string which is the name of the type of the
field as it appears in the source code. The exact contents and format of the
type name are not specified, but in practice will be the name of any valid
type for a field e.g.

- Concrete types e.g `"u32"`,`"bool"`,`"Foo"`etc.
- Type parameters e.g `"T"`,`"U"`
- Generic types e.g `"Vec<u32>"`,`"Vec<T>"`
- Associated types e.g. `"T::MyType"`,`"<T as MyTrait>::MyType"`
- Type aliases e.g. `"MyTypeAlias"`,`"MyTypeAlias<T>"`
- Other built in Rust types e.g. arrays, references etc.

Note that the type name doesn’t correspond to the underlying type of the field, unless using a concrete type directly. Any given type may be referred to by multiple field type names, when using generic type parameters and type aliases.

This is intended for informational and diagnostic purposes only. Although it is possible to infer certain properties e.g. whether a type name is a type alias, there are no guarantees provided, and the type name representation may change.

# Path in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.Path.html

## Expand description

Represents the path of a type definition.

This consists of several segments that each have to be a valid Rust
identifier. The first segment represents the crate name in which the type
has been defined. The last segment is the identifier accessed with `ident()`.

Rust prelude type may have an empty namespace definition.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.segments)

`segments: `[Vec](https://docs.rs/prelude/vec/struct.Vec.html)<T::[String](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.String)>The segments of the namespace.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/ty/path.rs.html#103-115)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/ty/path.rs.html#103-115)

Create a new Path

The `segment_replace` is a list of `(search, replace)` items. Every
`search` item that appears in the `module_path` is replaced by the
`replace` item. This can be used for example to replace the crate name
or even the name of the type in the final [ Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

- If the type identifier, module path or replace contain invalid Rust identifiers

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/ty/path.rs.html#163-170)

Does *not* check that the segments are valid Rust identifiers.

# PortableRegistry in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.PortableRegistry.html

```
pub struct PortableRegistry {
    pub types:
```
[Vec](https://docs.rs/prelude/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[PortableType](https://docs.rs/struct.PortableType.html)>,
}## Expand description

A read-only registry containing types in their portable form for serialization.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.types)

`types: `[Vec](https://docs.rs/prelude/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[PortableType](https://docs.rs/struct.PortableType.html)>## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the type definition for the given identifier, `None` if no type found for that ID.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/portable.rs.html#70-72)#### pub fn [types](https://docs.rs#method.types)(&self) -> &[[PortableType](https://docs.rs/struct.PortableType.html)]

Prefer to access the fields directly; this getter will be removed in the next major version

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/portable.rs.html#70-72)

#### pub fn [types](https://docs.rs#method.types)(&self) -> &[[PortableType](https://docs.rs/struct.PortableType.html)]

Prefer to access the fields directly; this getter will be removed in the next major version

Returns all types with their associated identifiers.

Retains only the portable types needed to express the provided ids.

The type IDs retained are returned as key to the [ BTreeMap](https://docs.rs/prelude/collections/struct.BTreeMap.html).
The value of the map represents the new ID of that type.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

A given type ID can be defined by nesting type IDs, such as the case
of a [ TypeDef::Composite](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeDef.html#variant.Composite) and others. To retain a valid

[all the types needed to express an ID are included. Therefore, the number of elements defined by the result equals or exceeds the number of provided IDs.](https://docs.rs/struct.PortableRegistry.html)

# TypeDefBitSequence in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.TypeDefBitSequence.html

`pub struct TypeDefBitSequence<T: `[Form](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html) = [MetaForm](https://docs.rs/form/enum.MetaForm.html)> {
    pub bit_store_type: T::[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type),
    pub bit_order_type: T::[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type),
}## Expand description

Type describing a [`bitvec::vec::BitVec`].

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

This can only be constructed for `TypeInfo` in the `MetaForm` with the `bit-vec` feature
enabled, but can be decoded or deserialized into the `PortableForm` without this feature.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bit_store_type)

`bit_store_type: T::`[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type)The type implementing [`bitvec::store::BitStore`].

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bit_order_type)

`bit_order_type: T::`[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type)The type implementing [`bitvec::order::BitOrder`].

Returns the type of the bit ordering of the [`::bitvec::vec::BitVec`].

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/ty/mod.rs.html#666-668)#### pub fn [bit_store_type](https://docs.rs#method.bit_store_type)(&self) -> &T::[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type)

Prefer to access the fields directly; this getter will be removed in the next major version

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/scale_info/ty/mod.rs.html#666-668)

#### pub fn [bit_store_type](https://docs.rs#method.bit_store_type)(&self) -> &T::[Type](https://docs.rs/form/trait.Form.html#associatedtype.Type)

Prefer to access the fields directly; this getter will be removed in the next major version

Returns underlying type used to store the [`::bitvec::vec::BitVec`].

Creates a new [ TypeDefBitSequence](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeDefBitSequence.html) for the supplied bit order and bit store types.

With the `bit-vec` feature enabled, the expected usage is to provide either
`bitvec::order::Lsb0` or `bitvec::order::Msb0` as the order type, and then something
like u8, u8, or u32 as the store type. Without the `bit-vec` feature enabled, it’s
recommended that your types have identical `TypeInfo` to those.

# TypeDefComposite in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.TypeDefComposite.html

## Expand description

A composite type, consisting of either named (struct) or unnamed (tuple struct) fields

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#a-rust-struct-with-named-fields)A Rust struct with named fields.

```
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age_in_years: u8,
    friends: Vec<Person>,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#a-tuple-struct-with-unnamed-fields)A tuple struct with unnamed fields.

`struct Color(u8, u8, u8);`[§](https://docs.rs#a-so-called-unit-struct)A so-called unit struct

`struct JustAMarker;`## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.fields)

`fields: `[Vec](https://docs.rs/prelude/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Field](https://docs.rs/struct.Field.html)<T>>The fields of the composite type.

# TypeDefVariant in scale_info - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scale-info/2.11.6/scale_info/struct.TypeDefVariant.html

## Expand description

A Enum type (consisting of variants).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#a-rust-enum-aka-tagged-union)A Rust enum, aka tagged union.

```
enum MyEnum {
    RustAllowsForClikeVariants,
    AndAlsoForTupleStructs(i32, bool),
    OrStructs {
        with: i32,
        named: bool,
        fields: [u8; 32],
    },
    ItIsntPossibleToSetADiscriminantThough,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#a-c-like-enum-type)A C-like enum type.

```
enum Days {
    Monday,
    Tuesday,
    Wednesday,
    Thursday = 42, // Allows setting the discriminant explicitly
    Friday,
    Saturday,
    Sunday,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#an-empty-enum-for-marker-purposes)An empty enum (for marker purposes)
